title: Review scrapbook — PR heuristics & follow-ups
content:
Context: quick personal dump while reviewing PR #12874 (kv-cache hotpath optimization). Lots of half-formed ideas below — treat as scratch.

Goals:
- Fast triage so reviewers can decide if change is low-risk or needs staged rollout.
- Capture small, safe follow-ups that reduce tech debt.
- Record experiments and validation steps for future perf regressions.

Quick triage checklist (my rapid pass):
- Diff size: ~210 LOC (mostly new helper + small loop) — low to medium.
- Tests: unit coverage added for the helper, but no integration/latency tests.
- Feature flags: none present — suggest adding a rollout flag.
- Backward compatibility: API surface unchanged.
- Dangerous ops: direct mutation of shared cache map — investigate concurrency guards.

Minimal repro steps I used:
1) run unit suite for serving-runtime with short sequence lengths (seq=128).
2) run load-local with 8 concurrent clients hitting kv-cache prefix path.
3) compare p95 token latency before/after.

Observed behavior:
- Micro-bench: 5-8% median improvement, but p95 slightly worse (+12%).
- Heap delta: small but steady growth over ~10k requests in local-run.
- Thread contention: contention metric spikes on mutex in cache helper.

Immediate hypotheses:
- The optimization moves some work into the fast path but introduces more frequent mutex holds under bursty workload.
- Cache eviction logic may now run under the same lock, causing stalls.

Small/fast follow-ups (safe to do as separate PRs):
- Convert the global mutex to a read-write where reads are common. (owner: @Mina)
- Add a simple feature flag 'kvcache_opt_v2' to allow gradual rollout and quick rollback. (owner: @Henry)
- Add an integration perf CI job that runs the load-local script with fixed seed and reports p50/p95. Link to job in PR template. (owner: @Luca)

Longer refactor ideas (not for this PR):
- Shard cache by key-hash to avoid giant lock. Needs batching changes across runtime.
- Move eviction to background thread with async queue — reduces latency impact but complex.

Tests to request in review:
- Add a concurrency unit test that simulates N workers touching cache, assert no deadlocks and max latency < Xms.
- Add a regression scenario to perf CI (see linked_artifacts for job).

Rollout plan suggestion:
- Canary: enable flag in dedicated infra for internal customers (10% traffic) for 48 hrs.
- Monitor: p95 latency, error rate, heap growth. Set automatic fallback to false positive threshold (p95 +10% sustained over 1h).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep PR small. If mutex change needed, prefer separate PR so this optimization stays reviewable.
- Ask author to annotate why eviction runs under lock (comment in code).

Open questions for author (put as review comments):
- Does the cache helper need to touch any external state that would be unsafe if executed outside lock?
- Why was the mutex chosen vs atomic-ops in first place? historical context? (link jira RED-4321)
- Are there memory safety assumptions around KV pointers that require the current ordering?

Action items (me):
- [ ] Draft small PR for feature flag + rollout boilerplate.
- [ ] Prototype rwlock change in a sandbox branch and run jitter tests.
- [ ] Add perf CI job description to infra repo and link in PR template.

Misc scraps (half-formed):
- Consider a per-request token-budget to avoid hot keys blowing through cache eviction.
- Could we use an epoch counter + copy-on-write when eviction happens to avoid blocking readers? Feels heavy.
- Slack thread: ping @infra-observability for a tracer that can mark lock hold times.

If I drop this and come back: first check p95 numbers from CI, then check if heap growth reproduces in staging. Otherwise, lean towards accepting with feature flag and follow-ups.

End of scrapbook dump.
